title: An unramified morphism is quasi-finite at every point
statement: Let $f:X\to S$ be a morphism of schemes [def-pc-scheme] which is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. Then $f$ is quasi-finite at every point $x\in X$ in the sense of [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1): there are an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}A=U\subseteq X$ containing $x$ and an affine open $\operatorname{Spec}R=V\subseteq S$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum] with $f(U)\subseteq V$ such that $R\to A$ is of finite type and quasi-finite at the prime $\mathfrak q\subset A$ corresponding to $x$ [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime]: with $\mathfrak p\subset R$ the prime below $\mathfrak q$ and $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ its residue field [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], the point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$ corresponding to $\mathfrak q$ is an isolated point. In other words, $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2).

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite), lines 7779-7788; its proof is Algebra, Lemma 02UR (algebra.tex, lemma-unramified-quasi-finite, line 41599), which uses Algebra, Lemma 00PK (lemma-isolated-point-fibre, line 30196) part (2) and Lemma 00UW (lemma-unramified-at-prime, line 41568)

proof.text: *Affine charts and an unramified ring map.* Let $x\in X$ and $s=f(x)$. Since affine opens form a basis of the topology of a scheme [def-pc-scheme], choose an affine open $V\subseteq S$ containing $s$ and an affine open $U\subseteq f^{-1}(V)$ containing $x$, with isomorphisms $V\cong\operatorname{Spec}R$, $U\cong\operatorname{Spec}A$ [def-weil-affine-spectrum]; then $f(U)\subseteq V$. By clause (2) of [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open] the restriction $f|_U:U\to V$ is unramified. Under the identifications, $f|_U$ is $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ for a unique ring map $\varphi:R\to A$ (every morphism of affine schemes is $\operatorname{Spec}$ of a unique ring map), and $\operatorname{Spec}\varphi$ is unramified, since it differs from $f|_U$ by composition with isomorphisms on both sides and being locally of finite type with open immersion diagonal [def-weil-unramified-morphism] is carried along isomorphisms of schemes. By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] (direction 'only if'), $A$ is a finitely generated $R$-algebra via $\varphi$ and $\Omega_{A/R}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. In particular $R\to A$ is of finite type. (Stacks, Algebra, Lemma 02UR: 'An unramified ring map is of finite type'; the passage from schemes to rings is Morphisms, Lemma 02V5, whose proof refers to Algebra 02UR.)

source.place: Morphisms, Lemma 02V5 (lemma-unramified-quasi-finite, lines 7779-7788) and its proof; Algebra, proof of Lemma 02UR (algebra.tex line 41599), first sentence

proof.text: *The fibre ring is unramified over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$.* Let $\mathfrak q\subset A$ be the prime corresponding to $x$ and $\mathfrak p=\varphi^{-1}(\mathfrak q)$ (the prime corresponding to $s$), with residue field $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, and let $F=A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ be the fibre ring [def-weil-pbc-localization-at-prime], a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra via $\lambda\mapsto1\otimes\lambda$. If $a_1,\dots,a_m$ generate $A$ as an $R$-algebra, then $a_1\otimes1,\dots,a_m\otimes1$ generate $F$ as a $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra (every $a\otimes\lambda=(a\otimes1)\lambda$ and $a$ is a polynomial in the $a_i$ with coefficients from $R$), so $F$ is a finitely generated $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebra. By [lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change] applied to $R\to R'=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $R\to A$, with $A'=\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA$, we have $\Omega_{A'/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}\cong\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_R\Omega_{A/R}=0$ by step 1; the swap $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\otimes_RA\to A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, $\lambda\otimes a\mapsto a\otimes\lambda$, is an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras, so $\Omega_{F/\kappa(\mathfrak p)}=0$ [def-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials]. Thus $\kappa(\mathfrak p)\to F$ is an unramified ring map (Stacks, Algebra, Definition 00UT), and by [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine] (direction 'if') the morphism $\operatorname{Spec}F\to\operatorname{Spec}\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ induced by the structure map is unramified [def-weil-unramified-morphism]. (Stacks, proof of Algebra, Lemma 00UW: 'The base change $S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is unramified over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ by Lemma 00UV', whose proof is the base change of differentials, Algebra, Lemma 00RV.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00UW (lemma-unramified-at-prime, line 41568), lines 41584-41586, with Lemma 00UV (lemma-unramified) and Lemma 00RV (lemma-differentials-base-change)

proof.text: *The fibre is a finite discrete space.* By [lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product] applied to $k=\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and $C=F$ (step 2), there are $n\ge0$, finite separable field extensions $L_1,\dots,L_n$ of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ and an isomorphism of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$-algebras $F\cong L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$. By [lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields] (2) the space $\operatorname{Spec}(L_1\times\cdots\times L_n)$ is discrete. A ring isomorphism $\theta:F\to L_1\times\cdots\times L_n$ induces the homeomorphism $\mathfrak Q\mapsto\theta^{-1}(\mathfrak Q)$ of spectra [def-weil-affine-spectrum] (its inverse is induced by $\theta^{-1}$), so $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is discrete: every one-point subset of $\operatorname{Spec}F$ is open. (Stacks, proof of Algebra, Lemma 00UW: 'Hence $F=S\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p)$ is a finite product of finite separable field extensions of $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$'.)

source.place: Algebra, proof of Lemma 00UW (lemma-unramified-at-prime, line 41568), lines 41586-41592, with Lemma 00U3 (lemma-etale-over-field)

proof.text: *Conclusion.* By [lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection] there is a unique prime $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ of $F$ with $j^{-1}(\overline{\mathfrak q})=\mathfrak q$, where $j:A\to F$, $a\mapsto a\otimes1$; by step 3 the set $\{\overline{\mathfrak q}\}$ is open in $\operatorname{Spec}F$, i.e. $\overline{\mathfrak q}$ is an isolated point of $\operatorname{Spec}(A\otimes_R\kappa(\mathfrak p))$. Since $R\to A$ is of finite type (step 1), this says by [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] that $R\to A$ is quasi-finite at $\mathfrak q$. With the affine opens $U\ni x$, $V$ of step 1 ($f(U)\subseteq V$), this is the condition of [pqf-def-quasifinite] (1): $f$ is quasi-finite at $x$. As $x\in X$ was arbitrary, $f$ is locally quasi-finite [pqf-def-quasifinite] (2). (Stacks, Algebra, Lemma 02UR, proof: 'apply the characterization of Lemma 00PK part (2) using Lemma 00UW'. Stacks deduces from 00UW that $S_{\mathfrak q}/\mathfrak pS_{\mathfrak q}=F_{\overline{\mathfrak q}}=\kappa(\mathfrak q)$ is finite over $\kappa(\mathfrak p)$, condition (2) of 00PK, and then condition (1) by the equivalence of 00PK; here condition (1) of 00PK, the definition [def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime] uses, is read off directly from the discreteness of the whole fibre $\operatorname{Spec}F$ shown in the proof of 00UW, which makes the equivalence (2)$\Leftrightarrow$(1) of 00PK unnecessary.)

Proof in four steps following Algebra 02UR with the proof of 00UW: (1) affine charts, restriction unramified (lem-weil-pbc-unramified-base-change-open (2)) and Spec-to-ring translation (leaf lem-weil-pbc-unramified-ring-map-iff-unramified-affine): R->A finite type with Omega=0; (2) fibre ring F=A(x)kappa(p) finitely generated with Omega=0 by the leaf lem-weil-pbc-kahler-differentials-base-change, hence Spec F -> Spec kappa(p) unramified; (3) F is a finite product of finite separable extensions (lem-weil-pbc-unramified-algebra-over-field-product) so Spec F is discrete (lem-weil-pbc-spec-finite-product-fields (2)); (4) the prime of F over q (lem-weil-pbc-fibre-ring-primes-bijection) is isolated: quasi-finite at q (def-weil-pbc-ring-map-quasi-finite-at-prime), i.e. pqf-def-quasifinite (1), for every x. Deviation from the letter of 02UR: Stacks goes through 00PK (2) (S_q/pS_q = kappa(q) finite) and the equivalence (2)<=>(1) of 00PK; here (1) is read off the discreteness of the whole fibre, which the proof of 00UW establishes, so no node for 00PK or 00PJ is needed.
